case_study_packaging.headline: Advantia Health unlocks $874K in annual savings and nearly 4× ROI through Treya-led strategic sourcing overhaul
case_study_packaging.client_problem_statement: Rapid growth and a recent acquisition left Advantia Health’s 40-plus women’s health clinics buying independently, paying inconsistent prices, and lacking the procurement discipline private-equity backer BlueMountain Capital expected. With $19 million in annual spend scattered across two AP systems and hundreds of suppliers, Advantia needed a fast, low-disruption path to improve margins and hit EBITDA targets.
approach_summary: Analyzed $19 M in AP and P-card data across 10 spend categories to size a $1.37 M savings opportunity portfolio.
Renegotiated the single-source Athena revenue-cycle contract, cutting fees from 3.39 % to 3.15 % and securing a $259 K annual reduction without triggering a $9 M termination clause.
Ran competitive RFPs and distributor consolidation, awarding Heartland region medical-supply volume to McKesson for a 14 % cost drop plus 60-day payment terms.
Performed make-versus-buy analysis on sonography staffing and guided a transition to an in-house recruiting model that lowers costs 19 % while maintaining imaging capacity.
Instituted enterprise-wide purchasing policies—such as 5-unit IUD order minimums and Bayer’s Confidence-in-Coverage program enrollment—capturing overlooked manufacturer discounts and credits.
case_study_packaging.value_delivered_blurb: Treya’s six implemented workstreams are already delivering $684,936 in locked-in annual savings, with another $189,484 in late-stage contracting—totaling $874,420 of recurring benefit. The results exceed the PE sponsor’s $450 K minimum‐savings guarantee by 94 % and generate a 3.9× return on Treya’s $225 K fixed project fee. Beyond dollars, Advantia now operates with standardized purchasing policies, extended supplier payment terms, and a clearer line of sight into spend across all 40 clinics.
where_we_were_unique: Captured first measurable savings within 45 days by targeting quick-win IUD purchasing policies.
Deep healthcare-provider expertise enabled fee reductions from a locked four-year Athena contract without service disruption.
Hands-on, clinic-level change management maintained physician and practice-manager buy-in during distributor and staffing transitions.
Outperformed the private-equity savings threshold, delivering nearly double the guaranteed amount and almost 4× ROI on consulting fees.
